finding.claim: Remote embed HTML is emitted unescaped, bypassing html_input escape/strip, so any page the embed adapter fetches can inject markup into rendered output when the embed extension is enabled without a domain allowlist.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied Markdown: a standalone line starting with https:// (src/Extension/Embed/EmbedStartParser.php:34-51). The adapter fetches that URL and stores the response's code->html (src/Extension/Embed/Bridge/OscaroteroEmbedAdapter.php:43-47).
finding.sink: src/Extension/Embed/EmbedRenderer.php:33 returns $node->getEmbedCode() raw, with no Xml::escape and no html_input check.

trace.note: Block start requires the line to begin with https:// and be a single link destination
Top-level embeds are passed to the adapter; non-top-level ones become plain text
Fetches each URL via embed/embed getMulti()

finding.guards_checked: Requires https:// (no javascript:/data:). Requires standalone top-level line. DomainFilteringAdapter (src/Extension/Embed/DomainFilteringAdapter.php:35-37) is only applied if the integrator wraps the adapter. Not guarded: html_input setting, escaping at render, and sanitising of code->html. Unverified: what the embed library puts in code->html (oEmbed/meta-derived iframes or scripts). The library source is not in this repo.
finding.repro: Enable EmbedExtension with OscaroteroEmbedAdapter and no DomainFilteringAdapter. Render an input line 'https://<attacker-host>/' where the attacker page's meta/oEmbed supplies HTML. Check whether the returned HTML appears verbatim in output despite html_input=escape.

finding.claim: The domain allowlist checks only the URL the author submitted, not the host actually fetched after redirects or after the fetch library re-parses the URL. An allowlisted host with an open redirect can make the server fetch an arbitrary host (SSRF), and the fetched HTML is then emitted (EMBED-1).
finding.source: Attacker-supplied URL on an allowlisted domain, e.g. https://allowed.example/redirect?to=http://169.254.169.254/ (EmbedStartParser.php:34).
finding.sink: Server-side HTTP fetch in OscaroteroEmbedAdapter.php:43 (embed/embed getMulti), which follows redirects.

trace.note: Filters on the submitted URL only
Host taken from PHP parse_url(); the fetch library may parse differently (e.g. backslash or userinfo edge cases)
Suffix match on '.'.$domain, so only subdomains of the allowed domain pass
Redirects and the final host are never re-checked

finding.guards_checked: Scheme must be http/https (line 47). Exact-or-subdomain host match (lines 52-58). Trailing dot stripped. Unverified: the embed library's redirect policy, whether it has its own private-IP guard, and its URL parser. Those are outside this repo.
finding.repro: Allowlist 'allowed.example'. Submit 'https://allowed.example/<open-redirect>?to=https://internal-host/' on a standalone line and observe whether the server fetches the internal host.

finding.claim: The mention identifier is inserted into the URL template without URL-encoding, so identifier characters such as / ? # can change the path, query, or fragment of the generated link.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled Markdown text matched by the integrator-supplied identifierPattern (src/Extension/Mention/MentionParser.php:49, 64).

trace.note: sprintf with the identifier as an argument; no encoding

finding.guards_checked: The template is developer-supplied, so the scheme is fixed and no format-string injection occurs (the identifier is an argument, not the format). The prefix must not follow a word character (MentionParser.php:59). Impact depends on the identifierPattern the integrator chose; a permissive pattern allows path traversal within the template's host.
finding.repro: Create a mention with template 'https://example.com/users/%s' and identifierPattern permitting '/'. Input '@../admin' or '@x?y' and inspect the href.

finding.claim: Defaults allow javascript:/vbscript:/file: links and raw HTML (allow_unsafe_links=true, html_input=allow). Any integrator who renders untrusted Markdown without setting these options gets stored XSS through link destinations and raw HTML.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled Markdown link destination, e.g. [x](javascript:alert(1)), or raw HTML blocks/inline HTML.
finding.sink: src/Extension/CommonMark/Renderer/Inline/LinkRenderer.php:47-50 emits href unchanged when allow_unsafe_links is true. HtmlBlockRenderer/HtmlInlineRenderer pass raw HTML when html_input=allow.

trace.note: Unsafe check is skipped when allow_unsafe_links is true

finding.guards_checked: Secure defaults are not applied. isLinkPotentiallyUnsafe() (src/Util/RegexHelper.php:251-259) works correctly but only runs when the option is false. Documented upstream behaviour, so this is a configuration risk rather than a defect.
finding.repro: Default Environment, render '[x](javascript:alert(1))' and ''. Both appear in the output.
